commands.title: Revert an agent run
commands.description: Undo an agent run's changes to this deck (or component master): the whole run, or only its last N changes (`lastOps`). Only that run's changes are undone — edits people (or other runs) made in the meantime stay, although an object the run created disappears together with anything added to it. Use it when the user asks to undo what you did; find the runId with agent.runs (or keep the one agent.startRun returned). It is the safety net, so it never asks for confirmation. It only works while the deck or master is loaded on the server (someone has it open, or a run on it is active): once the document unloads, or after a server restart, the run reports it is no longer revertible and the changes have to be undone by editing. Deck renames, sharing and other server-side actions of the run are not undone — only document edits.

commands.title: List agent runs
commands.description: List the recent agent runs on this deck (or component master), newest first: who asked, the request, when, how many commands ran and how many of them changed something, the status (open, closed, reverted) and whether the run can still be reverted (with the reason when it cannot). Covers runs of every agent session and user on the document, not just yours. Use it to find the runId to pass to agent.revert, or to tell the user what agents did to it. Read-only.

commands.title: Start an agent run
commands.description: Start a new run on this deck (or component master) for the user's current request, and return its runId. Call it once at the start of every new user request that will change the document ("make slide 3 shorter", "restyle the deck"), before the first edit, with the request in a short sentence. Everything you change afterwards belongs to this run, is listed under it in the Agent activity popover the user sees in the editor (deck or master), and can be undone as one unit with agent.revert — so one run per request is what makes "undo that" precise. Without it your edits still land in an automatic run per session and document (split after 10 minutes of inactivity), which lumps separate requests together. Starting a run closes your previous run on the same deck or master; it changes nothing in the document.

commands.title: Add animation
commands.description: Append an animation step for an object to the end of its slide's timeline. Omitted fields take the editor defaults: trigger afterPrevious, duration 0.6 s, delay 0 s, easing "power2.out"; moveTo targets the slide centre (960, 540) and rotateTo turns to 180°. Presets: fadeIn, fadeOut, slideIn, slideOut, scaleIn, scaleOut, zoomIn, rotateIn, bounceIn, flipIn, popIn, dissolveIn, wipeIn, moveTo, rotateTo. Triggers: afterPrevious (starts when the previous step ends), withPrevious (starts together with the previous step), onClick (waits for a click or the next key). The first step (step 0) with afterPrevious or withPrevious starts as soon as the slide appears; an onClick step 0 waits for the first click. Steps of older decks may read back as trigger onEnter (legacy: starts with the slide wherever it sits); it cannot be chosen, and a step keeps it until its trigger is changed. Rotation units differ by preset, as the animation engine defines them: rotateIn `angle` is in RADIANS (the starting offset, default -1.5708 = a quarter turn), rotateTo `angleDeg` is in DEGREES (the absolute end angle). Use animation.reorder to move the step, animation.update to change it.

commands.title: Remove animations
commands.description: Remove animation steps from a slide's timeline; the objects themselves stay. Deleting an object with object.delete already removes its steps.

commands.title: Reorder animations
commands.description: Set the play order of a slide's animation steps. `order` must list every step id of the slide exactly once (query.slide lists them). Triggers are kept, so an afterPrevious step now follows its new predecessor.

commands.title: Update animation
commands.description: Change an animation step: preset, trigger, duration (s), delay (s), easing, params. `params` is MERGED into the current params (a key set to null is removed; params: null clears them all). Changing `preset` drops params the new preset does not use and fills its defaults (moveTo: slide centre, rotateTo: 180°). The animated object cannot be changed here. Presets: fadeIn, fadeOut, slideIn, slideOut, scaleIn, scaleOut, zoomIn, rotateIn, bounceIn, flipIn, popIn, dissolveIn, wipeIn, moveTo, rotateTo. Triggers: afterPrevious (starts when the previous step ends), withPrevious (starts together with the previous step), onClick (waits for a click or the next key). The first step (step 0) with afterPrevious or withPrevious starts as soon as the slide appears; an onClick step 0 waits for the first click. Steps of older decks may read back as trigger onEnter (legacy: starts with the slide wherever it sits); it cannot be chosen, and a step keeps it until its trigger is changed. Rotation units differ by preset, as the animation engine defines them: rotateIn `angle` is in RADIANS (the starting offset, default -1.5708 = a quarter turn), rotateTo `angleDeg` is in DEGREES (the absolute end angle).

commands.title: Delete component
commands.description: Delete a component master from the folder. Objects already stamped from it stay on their slides (stamps are independent copies); it just cannot be stamped any more. Cannot be undone; confirm with the user first.

commands.title: Read component
commands.description: One component's master: its objects with every property (the shapes query.slide returns), its animations, its bounding box, and its slot map — every NAMED object is a slot; text slots show their placeholder text. Read it before component.stamp to know which slot names to fill. To change the master itself, target the component (componentId) with the ordinary document commands.

commands.title: List components
commands.description: The folder's components (id, name, thumbnail URL), oldest first. A folder keeps only a few — the blocks that recur on many slides, such as the headline block, the pagination or a card grid. Prefer them for those roles: component.get shows one with its slots, component.stamp places it. Do not expect a component for every layout; build one-off content from plain objects styled with the folder tokens.

commands.title: Rename component
commands.description: Rename a component of the folder. Stamps already on slides are unaffected. Undo: rename it back.

commands.title: Stamp component
commands.description: Place one of the deck's folder components on a slide and fill its text slots in the same step. The master's objects are copied as ordinary objects with fresh ids — rich text, groups and table content included; the master's animations are not copied — so editing the master later does not change this stamp. Without `at` the copy lands where the master was drawn (its bounding box top-left); `at` moves that corner. `slots` maps slot names (component.get lists them: the names of the master objects) to text: a plain string keeps the slot's formatting, { paragraphs } sets it explicitly. Returns the new object ids in stacking order. Use the folder's existing components for the roles they cover; do not stamp for one-off content. Access differs: stamping needs the editor role on the deck, but component.list and component.get are folder commands for the folder's owner only — an editor who does not own the folder cannot look components up, so ask the user which component to use.

commands.title: Who is editing
commands.description: Which decks of a folder people have open right now, and who (user id, email, name) — for example before a large change, to warn the user that colleagues are working in the deck. Decks nobody has open are left out. Folder owner only.

commands.title: Create deck
commands.description: Create a new, empty deck owned by the user — in `folderId` (one of their folders; folder.list) or, without it, in their Drafts folder. The deck already holds one empty slide (`firstSlideId`), so you can start editing it at once: target the returned `id` with slide.add, object.create, text.set and the other document commands. To start from a PowerPoint file use deck.importPptx instead. Undo: deck.delete.

commands.title: Delete deck
commands.description: Permanently delete the deck: its slides, speaker notes, collaborators, share links and uploaded media. Cannot be undone, and people who have it open lose it — always confirm with the user first, naming the deck. Owner only. To remove slides use slide.delete; to tidy up, deck.moveToFolder.

commands.title: Duplicate deck
commands.description: Copy this deck whole into a NEW deck the user owns: every slide (objects, rich text, tables, animations, speaker notes, outline), the deck guides and the media the slides show. Lands in `folderId` (one of the user's folders), else this deck's folder when the user owns it, else Drafts; in another folder, token references are rebound as deck.moveToFolder does. Sharing is not copied. Needs editor access to this deck. Returns the new deck — target its `id` to edit the copy. To copy only some slides into an existing deck use deck.insertFrom. Undo: deck.delete on the copy.

commands.title: Export PowerPoint
commands.description: Export the deck as a .pptx file, exactly as it is right now (including edits made seconds ago). By default returns a download URL valid for 15 minutes. It is a bearer link: anyone who has it can download the deck without signing in, so give it only to the user who asked (or fetch it yourself) — never put it in a slide, a share, or a message to someone else. `delivery: "base64"` returns the file inline instead, only for files up to 8 MB. Colour tokens are written as their colours; everything the PowerPoint format can hold round-trips back through deck.importPptx.

commands.title: Deck fonts
commands.description: Fonts bound to this deck itself — copies kept when a folder font the deck may use was deleted from the folder — with family, weight, style and a download URL. The fonts most decks use are their folder's: see folder.fonts.list. A family listed here or there can be used as fontFamily in text.

commands.title: Deck details
commands.description: The deck's record: title, folder, owner, thumbnail URL, created / updated times and the caller's role on it. It says nothing about the content — for slides and objects use query.deck and query.slide.

commands.title: Import PowerPoint
commands.description: Create a NEW deck in the folder from a .pptx file (public URL or base64): slides, shapes, text with its formatting, tables, images, videos, speaker notes and embedded fonts are converted to Narrative objects. Returns the new deck id and what could not be carried over (skipped shapes, unsupported images, ignored elements) plus the font families the slides use — upload missing ones with folder.fonts.upload. To add a file's slides to an existing deck use deck.insertFrom. A .pptx by URL or base64 is limited to 200 MB; larger decks import through the browser. Undo: deck.delete.

commands.title: Insert slides from a file or deck
commands.description: Insert slides into this deck at position `at` (0-based; omitted = at the end; past the end = at the end), taken from a .pptx file (URL or base64, at most 200 MB) or from another Narrative deck you can edit (optionally slides `from`..`to`, or exactly the slide ids in `slides`; copying needs the same editor access as exporting that deck, so a deck you can only view is refused). Slides keep their objects, animations, speaker notes, transition and background; their media is copied into this deck. From a deck in another folder, token references are rebound to this folder the way deck.moveToFolder does it. It is one change, reverted as one step. Returns the new slide ids — restyle them next if they should match this deck. For a new deck from a file use deck.importPptx.

commands.title: List decks
commands.description: Find decks: the decks the user can open — their own and those shared with them — most recently changed first, one page at a time. Each item is { id, title, folderId, updatedAt, role } (role = the user's role on it: owner / editor / viewer); `updatedAt` is the last change to its content, title or folder. Narrow it with `query` (title contains, ignoring case) or `folderId` (one of your folders; folder.list gives their ids) rather than paging through everything. A page holds `limit` decks (default 50, at most 200); when `nextCursor` is not null there are more — call again with `cursor: nextCursor` and the same filters. For a deck's full record use deck.get; to read its slides use query.deck.

commands.title: Move deck to folder
commands.description: Move the deck into another of your folders (folder.list), and rebind its design tokens to that folder: every colour / text-style / effect reference is pointed at the destination token with the same name (case and spacing ignored); a colour with no same-named token becomes its literal colour and a text style with none is detached (the text keeps its look), so the deck looks the same afterwards. Returns how many references were rebound, literalised and detached. Moving back does not re-link literalised colours, so confirm with the user first. Only the deck owner can move it, and only between their own folders.

commands.title: Rename deck
commands.description: Change the deck's title (what the deck list and the browser tab show). Slide names are slide.rename; text on slides is text.set. Undo: rename it back.

commands.title: Read the user's editor context
commands.description: Read what the user is looking at in their open editor on this deck: the active slide (id and 0-based index) and the ids of the objects they have selected. Call it whenever the user says "this", "here", "these", "the selected…" or "the current slide", then pass the returned ids to the edit commands — edit commands never act on "the selection" themselves. `open: false` means the user has no editor open on the deck (ask them which slide or object they mean). With several tabs open, the top-level fields describe the most recently active tab and `editors` lists all of them. Reads presence only; changes nothing.

commands.title: Link to present mode
commands.description: Get the URL that opens this deck in present mode, starting at a given slide (default: the first). Give it to the user when they want to present or preview the deck full screen; opening it needs their normal access to the deck. Presenting itself (next slide, fullscreen, presenter view) is done by the person, not by an agent. Changes nothing.

commands.title: Show something in the user's editor
commands.description: Point the user's open editor(s) on this deck at a slide and, optionally, highlight objects on it — e.g. after an edit, to show the user what you changed ("here is the new chart"). Each tab switches to that slide and selects the objects, flashing an outline around them for a moment; a show without `objects` clears the tab's selection. Nothing in the document changes and other people are not affected; only the calling user's own tabs receive it. If the user is busy in a tab — typing in a text box, cropping an image, editing path points or a table cell — that tab does not move: it shows a "Show" notice instead and switches only if the user clicks it within 20 seconds, so do not assume they are looking at it. `delivered` is the number of the user's tabs the request reached, not views that changed; 0 means no editor open on the deck — tell them where to look instead, or give them editor.present.link.

commands.title: Create folder
commands.description: Create an empty folder owned by the user, e.g. for a new client. Put decks in it with deck.create (folderId) or deck.moveToFolder, fonts with folder.fonts.upload. Undo: folder.delete.

commands.title: Delete folder
commands.description: Permanently delete the folder AND every deck in it, with their media, plus the folder's tokens, fonts and components. Cannot be undone; always confirm with the user first, saying how many decks go with it (folder.list shows deckCount). The Drafts folder cannot be deleted. To keep the decks, move them out first with deck.moveToFolder.

commands.title: Delete folder font
commands.description: Remove a font face from the folder (asset id from folder.fonts.list). Decks in the folder that the user owns keep a private copy so they still render; other decks fall back to another face. Confirm with the user first.

commands.title: Folder fonts
commands.description: The folder's uploaded fonts: family, weight, style, postscript name and a download URL. Every deck in the folder can use these families as fontFamily in text (text.set, text.format, object.update). Folder owner only.

commands.title: Upload folder font
commands.description: Add one font face (a TTF, OTF, WOFF or WOFF2 file, at most 10 MB) to the folder, from a public URL or as base64, so every deck in the folder can use it. Upload each weight / style as its own file. The file is parsed to read its family, weight and style; `fontFamily` binds it to another family name instead (e.g. the name an imported PowerPoint uses). A face whose postscript name the folder already has is refused. Only upload fonts the user has the right to use. Undo: folder.fonts.delete.

commands.title: List folders
commands.description: The user's folders, by name A→Z, one page at a time: { id, name, createdAt, deckCount } each. A folder is a client or brand: it holds decks plus the design tokens, fonts and components they share. Every user has a "Drafts" folder. Narrow it with `query` (name contains, ignoring case). A page holds `limit` folders (default 50, at most 200); when `nextCursor` is not null there are more — call again with `cursor: nextCursor` and the same `query`. Decks in a folder: deck.list with folderId.

commands.title: Rename folder
commands.description: Rename the folder. Its decks, tokens, fonts and components are unaffected. Undo: rename it back.

commands.title: Add guide
commands.description: Add an alignment guide to the deck. A vertical guide is an x position (0..1920 px), a horizontal guide a y position (0..1080 px). Guides are deck-wide and only help alignment in the editor; they never render in the presentation.

commands.title: Remove guides
commands.description: Remove alignment guides from the deck (every slide shares them). Objects do not move.

commands.title: Move guide
commands.description: Move a guide to a new position. Its orientation cannot change (remove it and add a new one). A vertical guide is an x position (0..1920 px), a horizontal guide a y position (0..1080 px). Guides are deck-wide and only help alignment in the editor; they never render in the presentation.

commands.title: Delete media
commands.description: Remove an asset from the deck's media library. Any slide object still showing it breaks (an empty image / video box), so first delete or re-point those objects (object.delete, object.update). Cannot be undone; confirm with the user first. Deck owner only.

commands.title: Font file URL
commands.description: A short-lived download URL of one of the folder's font files, with its family, weight and style (asset id from folder.fonts.list). Folder owner only.

commands.title: Video status
commands.description: Transcode state of an uploaded video — pending, processing, done or failed (with the error) — plus its duration, size and playback / poster / thumbnail URLs once done. Poll it after media.upload until `transcodeStatus` is "done" (typically seconds to a few minutes). Images and fonts need no processing: they are ready as soon as media.upload returns.

commands.title: Upload media
commands.description: Add an image (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF, SVG, …), a video (MP4, MOV, WebM, …) or a font file to the deck from a public URL or as base64, and get its asset id. It does NOT place anything on a slide: create an image or video object with object.create and this assetId (width / height tell you its native size). The file gets the same checks as a browser upload: size limits per kind (images 25 MB, videos 200 MB, fonts 8 MB — a larger video goes through the browser upload, up to 500 MB), at most 2 URL downloads at once per user, SVGs are sanitised, a file whose content does not match its type is refused, very large images are scaled down. A video is transcoded in the background: poll media.status until it is done before presenting it.

commands.title: Image URL
commands.description: A signed URL of one of the deck's images, in a size variant: thumb (small), preview, display (default, slide size) or original. Use it to look at an image a slide shows, or to hand it to the user. For videos use media.status; slide screenshots are query.render (planned, not available yet).

commands.title: Align objects to each other
commands.description: Align two or more objects to the edges or centre of their combined bounding box (e.g. 'left' moves every object's left edge to the leftmost edge). Rotation is ignored; cropped images keep their crop. To align objects to the slide itself use object.alignToSlide.

commands.title: Align to slide
commands.description: Move objects to an edge or the centre of the slide (1920 x 1080): `horizontal` left | center | right, `vertical` top | middle | bottom (give one or both). Several objects move together as a block — their combined outline is aligned and their layout among themselves stays; align them to each other with object.align. What is aligned is what you see: a rotated object's rotated outline touches the edge. A crop moves with its image.

commands.title: Create object
commands.description: Create one object on a slide: rectangle, ellipse, triangle, polygon, line, arrow, path, text, image, video or table. Only `type` is required; every property you omit takes the editor default (e.g. a 200 x 150 blue rectangle at 100,100). Text takes `text` as a plain string (blank line = new paragraph) or { paragraphs: [...] } with formatted runs and bullet/numbered lists. Images and videos need the `assetId` of an asset already uploaded to the deck (media.upload). A table takes rows/cols/defaults (same as table.insert) and is filled with text.set. New objects go on top of the stacking order; use object.layer to reorder. Units: the slide is 1920 x 1080 px, origin top-left, y down; x/y/width/height in slide px; rotation in RADIANS (90 degrees = 1.5708); opacity and *Alpha 0..1; colours as "#RRGGBB", a 0xRRGGBB integer, or a colour token { "$token": "colors.<id>" }.

commands.title: Crop image
commands.description: Change which part of a picture an image object shows; the object (its frame) stays where it is. In frame-relative px (0,0 = the frame's top-left): `set` places the whole picture at `picture` {x, y, width, height} (e.g. width 2x the frame = zoomed in 2x); `pan` shifts the picture by dx/dy; `zoom` scales it by `factor` around a point (default the frame centre; > 1 zooms in); `rotate` turns the picture inside the frame (degrees, or `relative`); `reset` removes the crop and the turn so the picture fills the frame. To change the frame itself while keeping the picture put, set x/y/width/height together with the current imageRect in one object.update.

commands.title: Delete objects
commands.description: Delete objects from a slide together with every animation step that targets them. Group members are deleted individually; pass every member to delete a whole group. To hide an object instead, use object.update with opacity 0. Locked objects are deleted like any other: `locked` is an editor-only flag that does not restrict commands.

commands.title: Distribute objects evenly
commands.description: Space three or more objects so the gaps between neighbours are equal, horizontally or vertically. The two outermost objects stay where they are. Rotation is ignored; cropped images keep their crop.

commands.title: Duplicate objects
commands.description: Copy objects on the same slide, offset by `offset` slide pixels (default 20, 20), on top of the stacking order, in one undo step. Copies get new ids and keep every property, rich text included. A duplicated group becomes its own new group (the original group is untouched); copying a single member of a group gives an ungrouped copy. A cropped image's crop moves with its copy, so the copy shows the same part of the picture. A copy of a locked object is locked too. Animations are not copied (add them with animation.add). Copying to another slide or deck is object.copyTo (planned, not available yet): today, read the object with query.object and recreate it there with object.create.

commands.title: Flip objects
commands.description: Mirror objects in place: `horizontal` flips left-right, `vertical` top-bottom. A flip toggles (flipping twice restores the original). A rotated object mirrors on the slide, as in the editor: its angle is negated along with the flip, so flipping both ways equals a 180 degree turn. For text the letters mirror too.

commands.title: Group objects
commands.description: Group two or more objects so they are selected, moved and duplicated together. Groups do not nest: every listed object leaves its current group for the new one, while members of that old group you did not list stay in it — to merge whole groups, list all their members (query.slide shows each object's groupId).

commands.title: Change stacking order
commands.description: Change where objects sit in the stacking (z) order of their slide: `front` / `back` move them to the very top / bottom, `forward` / `backward` move them past one neighbour. Several objects move as a block and keep their relative order. To put one object at an exact stacking position use `toIndex` (0 = backmost), which requires exactly one object. Other objects shift around the moved ones as needed.

commands.title: Move line ends
commands.description: Move the start (`p1`) and/or end (`p2`) of a line or arrow to points in slide px; an end you leave out stays where it is drawn. The box is refitted; rotation and mirroring stay. A line's stored p1 / p2 are relative to its box: for an unrotated line an end sits at (x + p.x, y + p.y). Returns both ends in slide px.

commands.title: Mask an image with a shape
commands.description: Clip an image to a shape's silhouette (rectangle, ellipse, triangle, polygon or path). The shape is consumed: it is deleted along with its animations, and the image's frame becomes the shape's bounding box while the picture stays exactly where it was on the slide. Shape rotation is ignored. Undo with object.mask.remove (which keeps the new frame).

commands.title: Remove image mask
commands.description: Remove an image's shape mask so it shows as a rectangle again. The frame stays where the mask left it and the picture does not move. Returns removed: false when the image had no mask. To remove a crop instead use object.crop.set with op reset.

commands.title: Move objects
commands.description: Move objects by a delta in slide pixels (the slide is 1920 x 1080, origin top-left, y down). This is the correct way to move anything: a cropped image keeps its crop. To place an object at absolute coordinates, set x/y with object.update (a crop follows there too) or compute the delta from its current x/y (query.object). To line objects up use object.align; to an edge or the centre of the slide, object.alignToSlide.

commands.title: Draw a path
commands.description: Draw a free-form path (what the pen tool makes) through `anchors` given in slide px; each anchor may carry bezier handles relative to it. The box is fitted around what is drawn. `object` sets the other properties: `closed: true` joins the last point to the first and lets `fill` show; with a `rotation` (radians) the points still land where given. For a straight two-point line prefer object.create with type line / arrow.

commands.title: Convert a shape to a path
commands.description: Turn a rectangle (rounded corners included), ellipse, triangle or polygon into an editable path with the same outline, so its points can be moved one by one (object.path.setAnchors). It stays the same object: same id, place in the stacking order, animations, group, fill (gradients and images too), stroke, shadow, rotation and mirroring. Shape-only settings (corner radius, number of sides) become the path itself.

commands.title: Set path points
commands.description: Edit a path's points in slide px: `moves` puts chosen anchors (by index in the path's `anchors`) at new points, their handles and every other anchor staying where they are drawn — the way to move one corner, rotated or mirrored path alike; or `anchors` replaces them all (handles relative to their anchor). The box is refitted while the path keeps its rotation and mirroring. Stored anchors are relative to the box: for an unrotated, unmirrored path an anchor sits at (x + anchor.x, y + anchor.y). Shapes convert with object.path.fromShape first.

commands.title: Resize object
commands.description: Resize one object. Give `width` and/or `height` (slide px) and the `anchor` that stays put (default topLeft; center grows it evenly on all sides) — measured along the object's own axes, so a rotated object resizes like dragging its handle. `keepAspect` derives the missing side from the current proportions (with only one side given it defaults to true when the object is aspect-locked). Alternatively give the whole new box, `x`, `y`, `width` and `height` (top-left of the unrotated box), instead of an anchor. A cropped image keeps showing the same part of the picture: the crop scales with the frame. A line, arrow or path scales its points (not its stroke width). Text reflows, it is not scaled.

commands.title: Rotate objects
commands.description: Rotate objects about their own centres, in DEGREES (clockwise positive): `degrees` is the new angle, or with `relative: true` an amount added to the current one. A cropped image turns with its crop. object.update sets the raw `rotation`, which is in radians.

commands.title: Ungroup objects
commands.description: Remove the given objects from their group. To dissolve a whole group, pass all its members (query.slide lists objects with their groupId).

commands.title: Update object properties
commands.description: ROTATION IS IN RADIANS here (the stored unit): 90 degrees = 1.5708, 180 = 3.1416; object.rotate takes degrees. Change properties of an object — fill, stroke, opacity, font size, corner radius, shadow, name, lock, x/y/width/height, rotation, … — validated against its type before anything is written (unknown keys fail). `null` removes an optional property. Use `updates` to patch several objects on one slide in one step. Not for tables' rows/columns/cells (table.* commands) or relative moves (object.move). Raw fields do exactly what they say and no more; where the editor does more, compose it yourself: (1) Setting x/y of a cropped image moves its crop along, but width/height do NOT scale the crop (`imageRect`) — resize with object.resize, which does. (2) `flipH` / `flipV` only mirror the content without negating `rotation` as the editor's Flip does — flip with object.flip. (3) Box-level typography (fontFamily, fontSize, fontWeight, color, …) is only the default: inline run formatting in the text overrides it, so a box-wide change on formatted text needs text.format with `clear` for those attributes first — put both in one ops.apply. (4) `fontFamily` does not snap `fontWeight` to a cut the new family has (the editor does); set a weight the family provides in the same patch. (5) `textStyleId` only links a folder text style, it does not apply it; set the style's font fields in the same patch; text.style.apply (planned, not available yet) will do both. `text` on a text box replaces the body with plain text (formatting is dropped; use text.set for formatted text, text.format for styling ranges). `locked` is an editor-only flag (it stops a person dragging, resizing or deleting the object on the canvas); it does not restrict commands, so locked objects can be changed and `locked` set or cleared like any property. Units: the slide is 1920 x 1080 px, origin top-left, y down; x/y/width/height in slide px; rotation in RADIANS (90 degrees = 1.5708); opacity and *Alpha 0..1; colours as "#RRGGBB", a 0xRRGGBB integer, or a colour token { "$token": "colors.<id>" }.

commands.title: Apply several edits at once
commands.description: Run a list of document commands on one deck as ONE change: collaborators receive one update and it is one step to revert. With `atomic: true` (default) either every op succeeds or nothing changes — all inputs are validated first, then the ops run in order, each seeing the result of the previous ones. With `atomic: false` failing ops are reported in `results` and skipped. Only commands that edit the deck document can be batched (not export, share, media upload or other server-side commands). Prefer this over many single calls whenever you make more than one edit.

commands.title: Deck outline
commands.description: A compact outline of the whole deck, built to fit a model's context: every slide with its id, 0-based index, name, a title guessed from its largest text, outline indent, skipped flag, transition kind and object / animation counts, plus the deck's alignment guides. Start here, then read one slide with query.slide. Slides are 1920 x 1080 px.

commands.title: Read object
commands.description: One object with all its properties (same shape as in query.slide) plus the animation steps that target it and its stacking position (0 = backmost). Use it before text.format / text.list to see the exact text offsets, or before object.update to see current values.

commands.title: Read slide
commands.description: Everything on one slide: every object with all its properties in stacking order (first = backmost), the animation steps in play order, the transition, the background (null = default white) and the speaker notes as plain text (slide.notes.get has them as Markdown with their formatting). Text bodies come as plain `text` (blank line between paragraphs) plus `paragraphs` with runs and list attributes when formatted; colours as "#rrggbb" or { $token }. For one object use query.object. It also reads a component master: target the component (componentId) and read slide { index: 0 } — edit the master with the same object and text commands.

commands.title: Cancel an invite
commands.description: Withdraw a pending email invite (id from share.invites.list): the link in the email stops working. Confirm with the user first.

commands.title: List pending invites
commands.description: Email invites to the deck that have not been accepted yet (id, email, role, sent and expiry time). An invite turns into a collaborator when the person signs in.

commands.title: Create a share link
commands.description: Create a link that opens the deck for ANYONE who has it, without an account, with the given role (usually viewer; an editor link lets strangers change the deck). Optionally expiring. Returns the URL to hand out. Confirm with the user first; revoke with share.links.revoke.

commands.title: List share links
commands.description: Active share links of the deck: anyone holding one opens the deck with its role, without signing in. Lists id, role, creation and expiry time; the URL itself is only returned when a link is created.

commands.title: Revoke a share link
commands.description: Revoke a share link (id from share.links.list): it stops working at once and people who opened the deck with it are disconnected. Confirm with the user first.

commands.title: Share with a person
commands.description: Share the deck with someone by email. If they already use Narrative they get the role immediately (`kind: "granted"`); otherwise a pending invite is created and an invitation EMAIL is sent to them (`kind: "pending"`), which they accept by signing in. Inviting an existing collaborator changes their role. Always confirm the address and role with the user first — this reaches a real person. To change the role of someone listed by share.permissions.list without emailing, use share.permissions.setRole.

commands.title: List collaborators
commands.description: Who has access to the deck: every collaborator with user id, email, name, role and when it was granted. People invited by email who have not signed in yet are share.invites.list; anonymous links are share.links.list.

commands.title: Remove a collaborator
commands.description: Remove a collaborator's access (user id from share.permissions.list); their open editors are disconnected. You cannot remove yourself, and the last owner cannot be removed. Confirm with the user first.

commands.title: Change a collaborator role
commands.description: Change the role of an existing collaborator (user id from share.permissions.list). Their open editors reconnect with the new role at once — a downgrade to viewer makes the deck read-only for them. You cannot change your own role. Sends no email. Confirm with the user first.

commands.title: Add slide
commands.description: Insert a new empty slide (white background, no objects, no transition). Omit `index` to append at the end; `index` is the 0-based position the new slide will occupy. To copy an existing slide with its content use slide.duplicate instead.

commands.title: Collapse slide section
commands.description: Collapse or expand a slide's outline children in the slides panel. Purely a panel view setting shared with collaborators; it does not hide anything from present mode (use slide.skip for that).

commands.title: Copy slides
commands.description: Copy one or more slides of this deck, as a block in their deck order, so the copies start at `index` (0-based position in the deck as it is now; omitted = at the end). Each copy is whole — objects with their rich text, tables, animations, transition, background, speaker notes, name — and keeps its object ids (Magic Move pairs them with the originals). The copies keep their relative outline levels, shifted so the first fits under the slide it lands below. To copy one slide right after itself use slide.duplicate; to bring slides from ANOTHER deck use deck.insertFrom.

commands.title: Delete slides
commands.description: Delete one or more slides with everything on them. A deck always keeps at least one slide: deleting the last remaining slide replaces it with an empty one. Outline children of a deleted slide stay and move up a level where they would otherwise be two levels below the slide above them. `landOn` is the slide an editor shows next: the nearest remaining slide above the first deleted one, else the first remaining slide. To hide a slide from the presentation without deleting it use slide.skip.

commands.title: Duplicate slide
commands.description: Copy a slide whole — objects with their rich text, tables, animations, transition, background, speaker notes, name and outline state — and insert the copy right after the source (or at `index`). Object ids are kept on purpose so Magic Move pairs objects across the two slides; use it before moving things on the copy to author a Magic Move.

commands.title: Set slide outline level
commands.description: Set a slide's outline indent level (0 = top level, max 6). A slide can be at most one level deeper than the slide above it, and the first slide is always level 0 — the same rules as dragging in the slides panel. Indented slides become children of the nearest shallower slide above them (sections); the outline does not affect present mode. Slides below it that would then be two levels deeper than the slide above them are raised with it.

commands.title: Move slides
commands.description: Move one or more slides, as a block keeping their current relative order, so the block starts at `toIndex` (0-based, counted in the deck BEFORE the move; clamped to the deck length). Outline children are NOT moved implicitly — list them too if they should follow their parent. `level` sets the outline level of the first moved slide; the others shift by the same amount, so the block's own structure stays. Afterwards no slide is more than one level deeper than the slide above it (deeper ones are raised), the rule the slides panel drags by.

commands.title: Read speaker notes
commands.description: A slide's speaker notes as Markdown with their formatting, in the syntax slide.notes.set takes; empty notes read as "". query.slide gives them as plain text — read them here before editing them with slide.notes.set so the formatting survives.

commands.title: Set speaker notes
commands.description: Replace a slide's speaker notes (what the presenter view shows) with Markdown: # headings, - and 1. lists (nested by indenting), > quotes, ``` code blocks, ---, **bold**, *italic*, ~~strike~~, `code`, <u>underline</u>, [links](https://…). A newline inside a paragraph is a line break; a blank line starts a new paragraph. "" clears the notes. The whole notes are replaced — read them first with slide.notes.get to change only part.

commands.title: Rename slide
commands.description: Set the name shown for a slide in the slides panel and the presenter view. An empty (or whitespace-only) name clears it, so the slide falls back to "Slide N".

commands.title: Set slide background
commands.description: Set a slide's background: { kind: "color", color, alpha? }, { kind: "linearGradient", angleDeg, stops }, { kind: "radialGradient", centerX, centerY, radius, stops } (2..10 stops of { offset 0..1, color, alpha? }) or { kind: "image", assetId, fit: cover|contain, dim? } for an already uploaded asset. Colours "#RRGGBB" or 0xRRGGBB. `null` resets to the default white. The whole background is replaced.

commands.title: Set slide transition
commands.description: Set how present mode moves INTO this slide: `kind` none | fade | push | cube | magic (Magic Move animates objects that share ids with the previous slide — see slide.duplicate), `durationMs` in milliseconds, `direction` left | right | up | down for push (null removes it). Fields you omit keep their value.

commands.title: Skip slide in presentation
commands.description: Mark a slide as skipped (hidden from present mode, still visible and editable in the editor) or un-skip it. Skipped slides do not count towards page numbers.

commands.title: Apply a table border preset
commands.description: Draw grid lines on a range of cells (default: the whole table) with a preset: all, outer (perimeter), inside (inner lines), insideH / insideV, top / bottom / left / right (that edge of the range), or none (hide the lines, overriding the default grid). `color` and `width` (px) are required except for none. For one individual line use table.border.segment.

commands.title: Style one table grid line
commands.description: Set or clear the style of ONE grid-line segment. A horizontal segment {orientation: "horizontal", row, col} is the line above row `row` in column `col` (row = number of rows is the bottom edge); a vertical one is the line left of column `col` in row `row` (col = number of columns is the right edge). `style: null` removes the segment so it falls back to the table default. Width 0 hides the line. For ranges use table.border.preset.

commands.title: Delete table columns
commands.description: Delete `count` (default 1) columns starting at `index` (0-based). The table shrinks by their size. Merged cells crossing them shrink; a merge whose top-left cell is deleted hands its text and style to the next cell of the merge. A table keeps at least one column — to remove the whole table use object.delete.

commands.title: Insert table columns
commands.description: Insert `count` (default 1) blank columns so the first new one sits at `index` (0-based; omit to append at the right). The table grows by the new columns, each as wide as the current average. Inserting strictly inside a merged cell extends the merge, as in PowerPoint. To set an exact size use table.resizeColumn.

commands.title: Insert table
commands.description: Insert an empty table of `rows` x `cols` cells (default 3 x 3) on a slide. Position and size are slide px (slide 1920 x 1080); without a size each cell is 120 x 60 px, split evenly. `defaults` restyles every cell at once (font, colours, padding, grid line). Fill cells afterwards with text.set using target.cell, and style them with table.style.*; do not use object.update for table structure.

commands.title: Merge table cells
commands.description: Merge a rectangle of cells into one cell. The range grows until it contains every merged cell it touches (whole merges only, as in PowerPoint), so check the returned origin and spans. The top-left cell shows its text; the other cells keep theirs hidden, and it reappears after table.split.

commands.title: Resize table column
commands.description: Set one column's width in slide px as drawn. By default the other columns keep their size and the table widens or narrows by the difference. With `keepTableSize: true` the table keeps its width and the difference comes from the next column (the previous one for the last column) — what dragging a boundary in the editor does. No column may end up smaller than 4 px.

commands.title: Resize table row
commands.description: Set one row's height in slide px as drawn. By default the other rows keep their size and the table grows or shrinks by the difference. With `keepTableSize: true` the table keeps its height and the difference comes from the next row (the previous one for the last row) — what dragging a boundary in the editor does. No row may end up smaller than 4 px.

commands.title: Delete table rows
commands.description: Delete `count` (default 1) rows starting at `index` (0-based). The table shrinks by their size. Merged cells crossing them shrink; a merge whose top-left cell is deleted hands its text and style to the next cell of the merge. A table keeps at least one row — to remove the whole table use object.delete.

commands.title: Insert table rows
commands.description: Insert `count` (default 1) blank rows so the first new one sits at `index` (0-based; omit to append at the bottom). The table grows by the new rows, each as tall as the current average. Inserting strictly inside a merged cell extends the merge, as in PowerPoint. To set an exact size use table.resizeRow.

commands.title: Split merged cell
commands.description: Split a merged cell back into its individual cells. `cell` may be the merged cell itself or any cell it covers. Each cell shows again whatever text it kept while hidden. Fails with conflict when the cell is not merged.

commands.title: Style a table cell
commands.description: Set or clear style overrides on one cell (fill, text colour, font size/weight, alignment, padding, …). Colours: "#RRGGBB", 0xRRGGBB or a colour token ref. `null` removes an override. For many cells use table.style.range, for the whole table table.style.table, for borders table.border.*, for the text itself text.set.

commands.title: Style a range of table cells
commands.description: Set or clear the same style overrides on every visible cell of a rectangle (e.g. colour a header row or a column). Cells hidden inside a merge are skipped; the merged cell itself is styled. Same fields as table.style.cell.

commands.title: Style a whole table
commands.description: Change the table-wide defaults every cell inherits unless it has its own override: font family/size/weight, text colour, alignment, fill, the default grid line (`border`) and padding. `null` clears an optional default. Cell overrides set with table.style.cell/range still win.

commands.title: Format text range
commands.description: Apply (`set`) and/or remove (`clear`) inline formatting — bold, fontWeight, italic, underline, color, fontFamily, fontSize — on part of a text box or table cell without changing the text. Choose the range by { match: "exact text", occurrence?: n | "all" } (safest) or { start, length } in characters of the text as query.object returns it; omit `range` for the whole body. `clear` runs first, so clear: "all" plus set restyles from scratch. Clearing makes the text fall back to the box defaults. For the box-wide font use object.update; inline formatting wins over the box defaults, so to restyle formatted text box-wide, clear those attributes here and set the box value with object.update in one ops.apply.

commands.title: Set list formatting
commands.description: Turn paragraphs into a bullet or numbered list, change nesting, glyph or numbering, or remove the list — on the paragraphs a range touches (omit `range` for every paragraph; a range of length 0 targets the paragraph containing it), exactly like the Inspector list controls. `kind`: "bullet" | "number" | "none" (removes the list and its level/glyph/numbering); `toggle`: the editor toolbar button (removes the list if every targeted paragraph already has that kind, else applies it); `level` 0..8 sets nesting, `indent` +1/-1 shifts it; `bulletChar` (implies bullet; null = default glyph), `numberFormat` (implies number), `startAt` (restart numbering; null clears). To write new list text use text.set with list paragraphs.

commands.title: Set text
commands.description:
Replace the WHOLE body of a text box or of one table cell (`target.cell`). Pass a plain string — a blank line ("

") starts a new paragraph, a single "
" is a line break inside the paragraph — or { paragraphs: [{ runs: [{ text, bold, italic, underline, color, fontFamily, fontSize }], list, level, bulletChar, numberFormat, startAt }] } for formatted runs and bullet / numbered lists (level 0..8). A plain string drops existing inline formatting and lists. Box-level typography (the box font, size, alignment) is unchanged — set it with object.update. To restyle part of the text without retyping it use text.format; for lists on existing text use text.list.

commands.title: Where a token is used
commands.description: Every place that uses one of the folder's design tokens: objects and text runs on each deck slide (deck, slide index, object, field), component masters, and — for a colour — the text styles whose colour is that token. Check it before changing or deleting a token to know what will change. Reads the saved documents, so edits from the last few seconds may be missing. Folder owner only.

allowlist.reason: Per-tab view state of one editor window; nothing in the document changes.
Per-tab editor preference, not document content.
Per-browser editor preference stored in localStorage.
Transient pointer mode of one editor; agents create objects directly.
Per-user editor state; agents address objects by id and read the user selection via editor.context.
Transient editor navigation state with no document effect.
Help overlay for humans; agents read tool descriptions instead.
Developer diagnostics overlay with no document effect.
Human presentation runtime, not document state; agents get editor.present.link to open a deck at a slide.

allowlist.capability: Browser sign-in and session (Google OAuth start/callback, current user, sign-out)
allowlist.reason: The interactive browser login that mints the session cookie. Agents never sign in this way: they authenticate with a personal access token (or MCP OAuth) and every MCP session is already bound to one user.

Credential management. An agent must not mint or revoke credentials: a leaked agent token that could create tokens would outlive its own revocation. The routes accept only the browser session cookie and reject any personal access token (apps/server/src/routes/accessTokens.ts).

Not a capability of its own: the HTTP transport that runs registered commands for scripts, exactly as the MCP server does for Claude clients. Everything it can do is a command in this registry, authorised and logged by the server host.

Not a capability of its own: the Streamable HTTP transport that serves this registry to Claude clients. Every tool is generated from a registered command and runs through the server host, which authorises, confirms irreversible commands and logs each op (apps/server/src/mcp/).

allowlist.capability: MCP OAuth authorization server (metadata, client registration, authorize, consent, token, revoke)
allowlist.reason: Protocol plumbing, not a user capability: how claude.ai connectors obtain a token for /mcp (RFC 9728, 8414, 7591, 7636, 7009), with the Google sign-in session as the login step. An agent never signs in this way; it is what gives the agent its session in the first place.
Credential management, like personal access tokens: an agent must not see or revoke the grants that give agents access. Session-cookie only (authPreHandler rejects every token).

allowlist.capability: Approving or declining an agent request (the confirmation page)
allowlist.reason: The human side of the human in the loop: a signed-in person approves or declines an agent call that needs their confirmation (irreversible commands, URL downloads). An agent must never be able to approve its own request, so the routes accept only the browser session cookie from Narrative's own origin and reject every token (apps/server/src/routes/agentConfirmations.ts).
Liveness probe for the Docker healthcheck and the reverse proxy; it reports no document or user state.
Operations telemetry (connection counts, document sizes) scraped by Prometheus with METRICS_TOKEN; not a user capability and deliberately kept away from user credentials.

Not a separate capability: a CRDT editor binding that writes the slide's notes Y.XmlFragment keystroke by keystroke, which no command could replay usefully. Agents read and replace the same fragment with slide.notes.get / slide.notes.set; the binding is the one editor write the one-door lint cannot see, so it is recorded here.
